features.claim: Velociraptor was a small to medium-sized dromaeosaurid.
features.quote: Velociraptor was a small to medium-sized dromaeosaurid, with adults measuring between 1.5–2.07 m (4.9–6.8 ft) long, approximately 0.5 m (1.6 ft) high at the hips, and weighing about 14.1–19.7 kg (31–43 lb).

features.claim: It was a slender, lightly built meat-eater.
features.quote: It was a slender, lightly built carnivore.
It was a bipedal, feathered carnivore with a long tail and an enlarged sickle-shaped claw on each hindfoot, which is thought to have been used to tackle and restrain prey.

features.claim: It had a long, low skull with an upturned snout.
features.quote: Velociraptor can be distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long and low skull, with an upturned snout.

features.claim: Its skull was elongated and grew up to 23 cm long.
features.quote: The skull of Velociraptor was rather elongated and grew up to 23 cm (9.1 in) long.

features.claim: Its snout was narrow and took up about 60% of the skull length.
features.quote: The snout, which occupied about 60% of the entire skull length, was notably narrow and mainly formed by the nasal, premaxilla, and maxilla bones.

features.claim: Its teeth were fairly equal in shape and had serrations, more strongly serrated on the back edge than the front.
features.quote: The teeth of Velociraptor were fairly homodont (equal in shape) and had several denticles (serrations), each more strongly serrated on the back edge than the front.

features.claim: It had a large hand with three long fingers ending in strongly curved claws.
features.quote: Velociraptor, like other dromaeosaurids, had a large manus with three elongated digits (fingers), which ended up in strongly curved unguals (claw bones) that were similar in construction and flexibility to the wing bones of modern birds.

features.claim: It had a sickle-shaped claw on its foot that could grow to over 6.5 cm long.
features.quote: This enlarged claw, which could grow to over 6.5 cm (2.6 in) long around its outer edge, was most likely a predatory device used to restrain struggling prey.
It was a bipedal, feathered carnivore with a long tail and an enlarged sickle-shaped claw on each hindfoot, which is thought to have been used to tackle and restrain prey.
Velociraptor was warm blooded and had feathers.

not_this.claim: Films and toys show it much bigger than it really was.
not_this.quote: As portrayed in the Jurassic Park movies, Velociraptor was recreated at twice its actual size and closely modelled on Deinonychus.

not_this.claim: Films and toys show it without feathers, but it really had them.
not_this.quote: Jurassic Park and its sequel The Lost World: Jurassic Park were released before the discovery that dromaeosaurs had feathers, so the Velociraptor in both films were depicted as scaled and featherless.

not_this.claim: Films and toys show it with the size, proportions and snout of Deinonychus, not of Velociraptor.
not_this.quote: They portrayed the animals with the size, proportions, and snout shape of Deinonychus rather than Velociraptor.

debated.claim: Some think Velociraptor may have been larger than the usual estimate.
debated.quote: Some estimates suggest that Velociraptor may have been larger, possibly reaching lengths of about 2.5 m (8 ft) and weighing up to 28 kg (60 lb).

debated.claim: The tail may have been more flexible sideways than once thought.
debated.quote: However, at least one specimen has preserved a series of intact tail vertebrae curved sideways into an S-shape, suggesting that there was considerably more horizontal flexibility than once thought.

second_reading.claim: It was warm-blooded to some degree.
second_reading.quote: Velociraptor was warm-blooded to some degree, as it required a significant amount of energy to hunt.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The idea that its feathers mean its ancestors could fly has been dropped.
second_reading.quote: This idea has since been discarded; the unmodified forearms count against it.
second_reading.why: the sentence does not support it

second_reading.claim: The feather specimen may not really belong to Velociraptor.
second_reading.quote: However, the specimen number has been corrected to IGM 100/3503 and its referral to Velociraptor may require reevaluation, pending further study.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: It may not have had a fully developed nasal thermoregulation apparatus like modern warm-blooded animals.
second_reading.quote: Tada with team suggested that Velociraptor and most other non-avian dinosaurs may not have possessed a fully or well-developed nasal thermoregulation apparatus as modern endothermic animals do.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it
